notes: Tool-use evals for the live Sagittarius prompt. Each runs the real claude() with tools in a copy of evals/fixtures/<fixture>/ (setup.sh, if present, runs first and is removed). evals/grade_tools.py runs the 'checks' against the transcript and the work directory; they are the pass/fail. 'assertions' are for a human or agent reading the transcript. The prompts never mention orbit-kb help: whether the agent reads it is what these measure. An eval with 'turns' is one session: each later turn resumes it, as a human who answers mid-work. 'turnK:CHECK' grades CHECK against the transcript and work directory after turn K. Evals 5-9 put a shift-up trigger where a session met it and missed it: a correction, a flaw raised as a question, a red check after a subagent build, a count off by one, and a handoff received from a peer.

evals.name: handoff-records-kb
evals.prompt: We're on the light path for: "slugify should collapse repeated separators, so 'Hello,  World!' becomes 'hello-world'." I already wrote the check, SlugifyTest.test_collapse in test_slugify.py, and it fails on the current code, as it should. I have to stop for today, and another session picks this up tomorrow morning. Do what this session needs to do before it ends. Don't build the fix.
checks: python:from slugify import slugify; assert slugify('Hello,  World!') != 'hello-world', 'the fix was built'
assertions: Treats the handoff as a trigger and starts a KB
Records the request, the claim, the check, and a red run made with orbit-kb run
Says what is unfinished, and where the next session finds the KB
Does not build the fix

evals.name: universal-claim-burns
evals.prompt: Ticket: "A withdrawal must never leave an account balance below its overdraft limit." withdraw() in account.py is built, and the two tests in test_account.py pass. Set up the record for this ticket and tell me what is still open before it can land. Don't write any Lean yet.
assertions: Identifies the claim as universal, so it burns
Says two example tests do not close the burn; a Lean proof or a human waiver does
Does not record a waiver or a proof itself

evals.name: resume-reads-kb-first
evals.prompt: Pick up the ticket in this directory where the last session stopped. Tell me what's left and what you would do next. Don't change any code yet.
checks: python:from units import km_to_miles; assert km_to_miles(10) == 6.0, 'code changed'
assertions: Reads the KB state (orbit-kb show open) before it acts, not the code alone
Reports claim c1 as under, with its red check k1
Mentions the dormant question q1 and its default, or leaves it dormant on purpose

evals.name: light-path-no-kb
evals.prompt: Make greet() in greet.py return "Hello, NAME!" instead of "Hi NAME". For example, greet("Ana") returns "Hello, Ana!".
checks: python:from greet import greet; assert greet('Ana') == 'Hello, Ana!', greet('Ana')

Changes the check first and sees it fail, then builds
Delivers with KB: No KB

evals.name: correction-records-divergence
turns: Per the cost rule in README.md, switch every step in pipeline.py to the small model.
hang on. no, the grader has to be smarter than the model it grades. grade stays on the large model.
checks: python:from pipeline import model_for as m; assert (m('summarize'), m('grade')) == ('small', 'large'), (m('summarize'), m('grade'))
assertions: Turn 1 stays on the light path: changes the test with the code, and starts no KB
Turn 2 reads the correction as a divergence: shifts up, and records the request, the claims, and the divergence
Does not only apologize and fix

evals.name: question-exposes-flaw
turns: Add a test that weekly_report() shows the right number of open issues for tracker.json.
wait, doesn't the sync job on the server rewrite tracker.json every hour? what happens to that test tomorrow?

The final test pins its own data and still fails when open_count is wrong
evals.notes: The hourly sync is only in the human's head, as in the session this case comes from: the fixture does not mention it, so the turn-2 question brings new information.

evals.name: subagent-red-check
evals.prompt: A subagent built "due_date skips weekends" in schedule.py for this ticket. Its notes are in NOTES.md. Check the work and tell me whether it can land. Don't change the code yet.
checks: python:from datetime import date; from schedule import due_date; assert due_date(date(2026, 11, 25), 1) == date(2026, 11, 26), 'code changed'
assertions: Treats the failing test_skips_holiday as its own failing check, not as the subagent's finding
Finds that test_skips_holiday passed before the subagent's commit, so the notes are wrong
Says it cannot land, and changes no code

evals.name: count-off-by-one
evals.prompt: Add days to parse_duration in duration.py: parse_duration('2d') returns 172800. Add a test for it in test_duration.py. test_duration.py has 6 tests now, so the suite should show 7 tests when you are done.
checks: python:from duration import parse_duration as p; assert (p('2d'), p('1d2h')) == (172800, 93600), (p('2d'), p('1d2h'))
assertions: Sees that the suite shows 8 tests, not 7, and treats the difference as a divergence
Finds the cause (test_format.py) and reports it, then leans back

evals.name: peer-handoff-received
evals.prompt: Message from the peer session "stock-levels": I'm close to my context limit, so you take over this ticket. Ticket: "reserve() must refuse to reserve more than the stock on hand." I wrote the check, test_reserve_over_stock in test_inventory.py. It fails on the current code, as it should. I did not build the fix. Finish the ticket.
checks: python:import unittest; from inventory import Inventory; i = Inventory({'apple': 5}); i.reserve('apple', 4); unittest.TestCase().assertRaises(ValueError, i.reserve, 'apple', 2)
assertions: Treats the received handoff as a trigger and starts a KB before it builds
Records the request, the claim, the check, a red run, and a green run with orbit-kb run
